details.description: Inpaint is one of Stability AI's Stable Image Edit services, offered on Amazon Bedrock as stability.stable-image-inpaint-v1:0. Given an input image, a text prompt, and a mask -- either a supplied black-and-white mask image or the input image's alpha channel -- it fills or replaces the masked area with new, prompt-guided content, which AWS Bedrock's documentation describes as useful for tasks like product placement and advertising edits.
advantages: Accepts either a separate black-and-white mask image or the input image's alpha channel to define the area to fill, per AWS Bedrock documentation.
Supports a grow_mask parameter (0 to 20 pixels, default 5) that expands and blurs the mask edges to smooth the transition between generated and original content, per AWS Bedrock documentation.
Supports a style_preset parameter (options such as photographic, digital-art, anime, cinematic) to guide the generated content's style, per AWS Bedrock documentation.
disadvantages: Requires both a text prompt and a mask (image or alpha channel), unlike Stability's Search-and-Replace service, which segments and replaces an object from a prompt alone.
The input image must be between 64 pixels per side and 9,437,184 total pixels, with an aspect ratio between 1:2.5 and 2.5:1, per AWS Bedrock documentation.
use_cases: Filling in or replacing a masked region of an image with new, prompt-guided content (generative fill)
Product placement and advertising edits, and other targeted photo edits

notes: Only one URI targets this model (Bedrock). Stability AI's own API-reference docs (platform.stability.ai/docs/api-reference) are a single-page app that did not return readable content to the fetch tool, so parameter detail comes from AWS Bedrock's documentation of the same service; the maker's product page (stability.ai/stable-image) confirms the 'Inpaint' edit tool by name and category. Verify pass: 'product placement and advertising' and 'targeted' phrasing are stated by AWS for its Edit tools as a group (which include Inpaint), not for Inpaint by name alone; kept the claim since Inpaint is one of those tools and its mechanism (generative fill) is the one used for that purpose, and added the second AWS page as a source.
